== Multiple winners ==
Ten directors or director duos have won the award twice. Three of them (<sup>{{double dagger|alt=Consecutive films}}</sup>) have won for consecutive films.<ref name="multiplepalme">{{cite web |last=Pineda Pacheco |first=Diego |url=https://collider.com/directors-with-two-palme-dor-cannes/ |title=All 9 Directors Who Have Won 2 Palme d'Or, from Coppola to Östlund |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=24 May 2023 |access-date=20 July 2023 |archive-date=26 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526190745/https://collider.com/directors-with-two-palme-dor-cannes/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/film/festivals/cannes-film-festival-2016-winners-palme-d-or-1201780561/ |title=Cannes: Ken Loach Wins His Second Palme d'Or for 'I, Daniel Blake' |last1=Lodge |first1=Guy |last2=Gleiberman |first2=Owen |author2-link=Owen Gleiberman |date=22 May 2016 |website=Variety |access-date=23 May 2016 |archive-date=23 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423063553/https://variety.com/2016/film/festivals/cannes-film-festival-2016-winners-palme-d-or-1201780561/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
